derived.prompt: Kepler-22b orbits the star Kepler-22, and Kepler-22 is located in the Milky Way. Does it follow that Kepler-22b is located in the Milky Way?
bridge: Kepler-22b orbits the star Kepler-22, and Kepler-22 is located in the Milky Way.
chain: Kepler-22b orbits the star Kepler-22. (given in prompt)
Kepler-22 is located in the Milky Way. (given in prompt)
A planet can lie outside the galaxy that contains the star it orbits. (edit)
So Kepler-22b being in the Milky Way no longer follows: no.

derived.prompt: Proxima Centauri b orbits the star Proxima Centauri, and Proxima Centauri is located in the Milky Way. Given only these facts, could Proxima Centauri b be located outside the Milky Way?
bridge: Proxima Centauri b orbits the star Proxima Centauri, and Proxima Centauri is located in the Milky Way.
chain: Proxima Centauri b orbits the star Proxima Centauri. (given in prompt)
Proxima Centauri is located in the Milky Way. (given in prompt)
A planet can lie outside the galaxy that contains the star it orbits. (edit)
So nothing given places Proxima Centauri b in the Milky Way: yes, it could lie outside.

The Sun is a planet..why: Deliberately false so the disjunction turns on the edited property: the Sun is a star.

notes: RBox revision of the topic's role chain: orbits ∘ located_in ⊑ located_in (a planet is in the galaxy its star is in: two different relations give a third) is removed. The chain rests on spatial containment, not on two names for one quantity. The instances are real exoplanets (Kepler-22b, Proxima Centauri b) whose galaxy is rarely stated for the planet itself. The chain tag is not on orbits' row in RELATIONS.md. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the first instance asks 'does it follow' (yes, then no), the second 'given only these facts, could it lie outside' (no, then yes). The near query is a chain through 'antiparticle of' and 'has charge' (yes). hops counts the instance facts in the prompt as one bridge (1 + 1).
